provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — inbound ZIP-wrapped macro-enabled documents and their detonation behavior (Word spawning macro/network activity) are detectable at the mail gateway and via office-child-process telemetry
medium — outbound document-template fetches to URL shorteners are detectable via proxy/DNS logs correlated with Office processes, but shortener use blends with benign traffic
medium — user-opened lure documents/executables are detectable via office-application child-process spawning and execution of files masquerading as Flash/Office/PDF, but depend on the user action

medium — remote-template loads (settings.xml.rels referencing an external URL) and Office reaching out to shortener/remote hosts on document open are detectable via document inspection and office-network telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — VBA macro execution spawning script/PowerShell children is detectable via office-macro and child-process telemetry (AMSI, Sysmon EID 1)

high — PowerShell script-block/module logging (EID 4104) captures the fmx.ps1 loader, base64 decoding of sdmc.jpg, cloud downloads and RC4 image reconstruction; Word/Office spawning powershell.exe is a strong lineage signal

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — cmd.exe spawned by Office/loader processes to stage payloads is detectable via process-creation and command-line telemetry
medium — a Python interpreter/.pyc executing from an unusual path under a RAT process is detectable via process-lineage and image-load telemetry, but requires Python-runtime presence

detection_candidates.technique_name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Compiled HTML File
detection_candidates.rationale: high — hh.exe processing a .chm that spawns a shell/downloader is a rare, high-fidelity behavior detectable via process-lineage (hh.exe -> cmd/powershell) telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: high — creation/modification of CurrentVersion\Run values (Sysmon EID 13, autoruns) pointing to loader/RAT paths is a directly observable, high-fidelity persistence signal

detection_candidates.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Launch Agent
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — new/unusual LaunchAgent plists invoking java are detectable via file-integrity monitoring on LaunchAgents and endpoint telemetry, but require macOS visibility

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: XDG Autostart Entries
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — new .desktop autostart entries invoking java from a user path are detectable via file-integrity monitoring on ~/.config/autostart, but require Linux endpoint visibility

high — the hollowing sequence (CreateProcess suspended, unmap, WriteProcessMemory, SetThreadContext/ResumeThread) into iexplore.exe, and iexplore.exe with anomalous network/parentage, are detectable via EDR process-injection and image/memory telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Software Packing
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — UPX-packed sections and packer signatures are detectable via static scanning and entropy analysis, but packing alone is common and requires corroboration

medium — PowerShell reading pixel data from a PNG to reconstruct code is detectable via script-block logging and anomalous image-parsing behavior, but the images themselves are valid and evade content filters

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — high-entropy encoded/encrypted artifacts are detectable via entropy and decoding heuristics, but require dedicated file inspection
medium — runtime base64/RC4 decoding by PowerShell is visible in script-block logs (FromBase64String, byte-array XOR/RC4 patterns), but decoding is common and needs context
medium — a valid signature reduces alerting, but the specific abused signer/thumbprint can be watchlisted and signed-but-anomalous binaries flagged via signer-reputation and behavioral analytics
medium — deletion of just-downloaded staging files shortly after execution is detectable via file-creation/deletion telemetry correlated with the PowerShell loader, but is a brief window
medium — file/directory enumeration is common; meaningful mainly within the RAT's process lineage and recon burst

detection_candidates.technique_name: System Network Configuration Discovery: Internet Connection Discovery
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — outbound requests to public-IP-lookup services shortly after implant start are detectable via proxy/DNS telemetry correlated with the RAT process
medium — drive/device enumeration by a non-system process is detectable in behavioral telemetry but is low-signal without process context

medium — bulk reads/staging of user document and picture folders by a RAT are detectable on Windows via file-access telemetry; the Android/Pallas PII collection is a mobile-threat-defense hunt candidate
high — repeated screen-capture API usage (BitBlt/GDI) by a non-interactive process is detectable via EDR behavioral analytics
high — low-level keyboard hooks (SetWindowsHookEx) and keylog buffer files created by a RAT are detectable via EDR API-hooking and file-write telemetry
medium — microphone-access APIs invoked by a background process are detectable on Windows via EDR; the Android/Pallas audio recording is a mobile hunt candidate
medium — webcam-device access by a non-conferencing process is detectable on Windows via EDR device-access telemetry; Android camera capture is a mobile hunt candidate
high — the distinctive Base64+'&&&&'-suffixed HTTP payloads and beacons to the listed C2 domains are detectable via network/proxy inspection and IDS signatures
medium — raw TCP sessions to actor C2 on non-standard ports are detectable via netflow/egress anomaly analytics but lack protocol-layer signatures
medium — encryption hides content, but the hardcoded AES-CFB IV (0123456789123456) is a strong hunt/attribution pivot for sample and traffic analysis
high — payload downloads following PowerShell/RAT activity, with subsequent file writes and execution, are detectable via process+network+file telemetry
medium — outbound data transfers to actor C2 over the RAT channel are detectable via egress-volume anomaly analytics tied to the C2 destinations, but blend into the encrypted channel

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — domain registration is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via passive DNS, registrar/WHOIS pivoting and infrastructure clustering on shared registrars and TLD patterns
low — capability development is off-victim; intel candidate via sample clustering and code/config reuse (AES-CFB IV, command opcodes)
low — certificate acquisition is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via certificate-transparency and signer-reputation tracking (the downstream signed binary is where endpoint detection lands)
low — payload staging on legitimate cloud hosting is off-victim and blends with normal cloud traffic; hunt candidate via egress to cloud-hosting following macro/PowerShell activity
low — adversary-controlled distribution site is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via infrastructure tracking and app-store/sideload telemetry (mobile)
low — social-media/messaging delivery occurs off enterprise telemetry; intel/hunt candidate via user reporting and brand/persona monitoring (mobile-centric)
low — mobile sideload/watering-hole delivery is largely outside enterprise endpoint telemetry; hunt candidate via mobile-threat-defense and web-filtering (mobile)
low — link-driven mobile app installation is outside standard enterprise endpoint telemetry; hunt/intel candidate (mobile)
low — direct API use is ubiquitous and only meaningful in combination with the injection/hollowing sequence; hunt candidate via API-sequence/behavioral analytics
